instructions: Mix the 2 cups masa harina and 3/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl. Add 1 1/4 cups hot tap water and 1 tsp of the oil and mix, then knead it in the bowl for 1 to 2 minutes, until it feels soft and smooth like play dough. If it cracks at the edges, work in more water 1 tbsp at a time. If it sticks to your hands, add a pinch more masa.
Cover the bowl with a damp kitchen towel and let the dough rest for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make a quick pico de gallo. Dice the 2 tomatoes, finely dice half the onion and chop about 1/4 cup of the cilantro. Toss them in a bowl with the juice of half the lime and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Cut the other half of the lime into wedges.
Shred a quarter of the lettuce and crumble the 4 oz queso fresco.
Mince the garlic clove. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a small saucepan over medium, add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Add the can of refried beans and 3 tbsp water and stir for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're hot and smooth. Cover and keep them on the lowest heat.

Divide the dough into 12 balls and keep them under the towel. Press each one between two pieces of plastic (a zip-top bag cut open works) with a tortilla press or the bottom of a heavy dish, into a round about 3 1/2 inches across and 1/4 inch thick.

Heat a large dry skillet over medium-high. Cook the rounds 4 at a time for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until the underside has brown spots and lets go of the pan. Flip them and cook the other side for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes.

While each one is still hot, hold it in a folded kitchen towel and pinch up a 1/2 inch rim all the way around the edge. They're hot, so the towel protects your fingers. Cook and pinch the rest the same way.
Pour the rest of the oil into the skillet and heat it over medium. Fry the sopes flat side down, in batches, for 2 to 3 minutes, until the bottoms are golden and crisp. Drain them on paper towels.
Taste the beans and the pico. If either is flat, add a pinch more salt, or a squeeze of the lime to the pico.
Halve, pit and slice the avocado. Spread a spoonful of beans into each sope, then top with the lettuce, pico, queso fresco and avocado, and drizzle over the 1/2 cup crema.
method_notes: All three make the dough from about 2 cups masa harina to 1 1/4 to 1 3/4 cups water and a little salt, shape 12 thick rounds about 1/4 inch thick and pinch up a rim. Tasting Table adds a teaspoon of oil to the dough, rests it 15 minutes, bakes the rimmed rounds at 400°F for 5 minutes and tops them with refried beans, cheddar, lettuce, tomato, red onion and avocado. Maricruz Avalos and Gonna Want Seconds cook the rounds on a hot griddle first and pinch the rim while they're hot, and Gonna Want Seconds then fries them in lard until golden and adds crema. This one follows Tasting Table's dough and toppings, cooks the sopes on the griddle and gives them a shallow fry so the masa cooks through and the base is crisp, and uses queso fresco in place of cheddar.
